empirical_structure_anchor.source: Hiraiwa-Ushimaru 2024 source-native archive acquired in PR #90
empirical_structure_anchor.observed_fdq_result: FDQ remains positive after site/season fixed effects, full functional-covariate adjustment, mainland exclusion, and Oshima exclusion.
empirical_structure_anchor.anchor_boundary: The empirical archive anchors dimensions and the need for a direct dependency endpoint. It does not provide true dependency values or an empirical dependency x FDQ interaction.

simulation.effect_scale: standardized outcome units per 1-SD FDQ change across a full 0-to-1 dependency contrast
simulation.inference: taxon + site + season additive fixed effects; site-season clustered sandwich SE; scenario-specific empirical null critical value
simulation.coverage_rule: Each synthetic replicate retains every taxon and every site-season cluster, then samples the remaining rows to the declared coverage fraction.
simulation.assumption_boundary: All coefficients, dependency supports, reliabilities, error scales and prospective coverage fractions are synthetic sensitivity assumptions, not estimates from the Izu archive.

scenarios.description: Current-structure diagnostic: nine eligible survivor taxa, 105 rows, a truncated synthetic dependency range, and proxy-like reliability.
Double seasons while retaining the same truncated dependency support, proxy reliability, and sparse coverage fraction.
Add four sites while retaining the same truncated dependency support, proxy reliability, and sparse coverage fraction.
Direct dependency measurement and denser matched sampling, but no extension of the synthetic dependency range.
Add one directly measured high-dependency endpoint to the narrow survivor-like support.
Ten directly measured taxa spanning the synthetic dependency scale with matched half-panel coverage.
Sixteen directly measured taxa, but still restricted to the narrow synthetic dependency range.
Sixteen directly measured taxa spanning the synthetic dependency scale.

design_contrasts.interpretation: Information gained by doubling seasons without repairing dependency support.
Information gained by adding sites without repairing dependency support.
Information gained by direct measurement and denser sampling while dependency support stays narrow.
Increment from adding one high-dependency endpoint after measurement improves.
Increment from filling the dependency gradient rather than relying on one endpoint.
Dependency-range information at fixed taxon count and coverage.

claim_boundary: This simulation ranks prospective designs under declared synthetic alternatives. It does not estimate empirical power, an empirical dependency x FDQ coefficient, historical selection, Bombus causation, or a causal Oshima-Toshima boundary effect.
